subject: api
text: No served network API exists — no TCP or UDP port; the one listener is local: the driver session's Unix-domain socket `{state_dir}/session.sock`, bound at one site since 2026-10-07-driver-session and serving the lifecycle (`hello`, `stop`) and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, driver calls and their answers (`call`, wire `v3` since 2026-10-19-session-recording, its replies including the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed`) (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:109-124; its row is below). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `escher-session mcp` role also serves the driver's verbs as MCP tools — twelve: the tenth, `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), answered by the server itself from the schema's fixed tables and running nothing on a session, the eleventh, `screenshot`, and the twelfth, `lint` — over its own stdin and stdout — no listener, port or socket, so the session socket stays the one listener — bounded by a 65,536-byte request line, a 1,048,576-byte tool result (one that holds an image measured by its whole written form, a text-only one by its text) and the idle expiry checked when a request arrives (the Input Validation MCP server row; the crossing ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»). In the slices that searched, as adopted, server routes or listeners are observed absent — searched: `TcpListener|listen\(` over the 32 s10 files — and a served API is observed absent — searched: `TcpListener|TcpStream|bind\(|listen\(` over the 12 listed s13 files. The controls below govern outbound requests and in-document navigation.

subject: api
text:
- **Control:** Settle and loads in flight
  - **Configuration:** A harness settle (`Harness::settle`) reports a load in flight at once — `NotSettled` naming the class `Loads` — and never waits on one: it waits on no clock and moves none — its `animating` reading reads the overlay scrollbar fade off the document's clock — so the absent request timeout above cannot hang it, and its pass loop is bounded at 64 passes; the driver's acting step over it (`Session::act` and the executor's settled step, so `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` on every carrier) settles again every 10 ms while the answer is `Loads`, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, 5 s of wall time under the 30 s answer read below, moving no time on the held instance, then returns the load still in flight as `settled: false` with its busy class — so the absent timeout cannot hang a command either, `LOAD_WAIT` ending every wait (since 2026-10-20-load-wait); the outcome is a returned value naming a class only — no URL, request, node, id, name or value — and the counter it reads stores counts only (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:15-28; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:60-127; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:151-186; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/report.md); the driver's command schema keeps this: none of its eight instance-level verbs has an argument or a result field of a wait — the seventh, `screenshot`, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, taking one optional `id` and answering `width`, `height` and `png`, a shot resolving at the harness's own time with no tick and no pump, so it moves no time, and the eighth, `lint`, taking no argument and answering `findings`, running no step and settling nothing, so it moves none either; the overlay scrollbar fade reads the document's clock
 — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, which only `tick`, `advance_time` and the driver's `advance` move — so two shots of one state read the same pixels until an `advance` moves the fade, a document built with no clock still fading by wall time (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:37-103) — nor do the three session-level verbs, whose one argument is `app` and whose result fields are `label`, `pid`, `served`, `idle_expiry_s` and `stopped`, nor, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help`, which takes no argument and whose seven result fields are fixed tables — and its validation reads no clock; the command line's own bounds, 30 s for a started host to answer and 30 s on each read of a call's answer, bound a transport and wait on no load; a step that ran and did not go quiet is a result (`settled: false` with its busy class) and not a refusal, and time on a held instance moves only when a caller asks for it with `advance`, 1 to 60000 ms a call — an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the bound the `settled` field's help states, and `snapshot`, `screenshot` and `lint` wait on none — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema/report.md; the wait has one served witness on the stand, the load page (`stand::boot_load`, `escher-session start load`): its one fetch of the fixed `http://stand.test/load.css` is answered in process by `LoadNet` after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms) from a thread of its own with fixed CSS bytes — no `blitz_net`, socket, listener, print or env read — and, `LoadNet` overriding no `is_noop`, the harness counts the load and the page's click waits it out within `LOAD_WAIT` (`stand_load_page`); every other stand boot holds `net_provider: None` (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:141-175)
  - **Stack reference:** blitz-test-harness · escher-driver

subject: api
text:
- **Control:** Local session socket (escher-driver)
  - **Configuration:** Reachable by the owning user only (state directory `0700`, socket file `0600`, a directory open to its group or to others refused); no handshake secret, token or peer-credential check; one connection at a time, a 2 s read and write bound and 30 s on a client's read of a call's answer, a request line of at most 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply of at most 128 and an answer of at most 1,048,576 on its JSON line — over it the reply is `oversize`, read by the client as `AnswerTooLarge`; `stop` removes the socket and the directory; since 2026-10-10-driver-cli a host that has answered no request for its idle expiry — `IDLE_EXPIRY`, 1,800 s, `serve`'s third parameter — ends exactly as on `stop`, every answered request, a refused or malformed one and an `attach` or a `status` included, counting toward `served` and starting the count again, a connection that breaks before its request is whole doing neither, and an expiry, like a `stop`, writing no record (the founder's answer to the orphaned-host question, 2026-10-10, relayed by the overseer; until then a host whose client died without `stop` kept running) (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:36-214; packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:15-27)
  - **Stack reference:** `std::os::unix::net::UnixListener`
